1.title: Jeremiah's call
1.text: A priest of Anathoth, Jeremiah prophesied for about 40 years, until Jerusalem's fall.

1.question: According to 1:5, what did God do before forming Jeremiah in the womb?
options: Waited for him to first become a priest in Anathoth
He knew him and ordained him a prophet to the nations
Promised to send him first to the distant land of Egypt
Chose his father Hilkiah to be a prophet instead

1.question: The mission of 1:10 includes rooting out and pulling down, and also?
options: Comforting and forgiving
Building and planting
Gathering and scattering
Teaching and baptizing

1.question: What vision does Jeremiah see, facing the north (1:13)?
options: A flowering olive branch
A boiling pot
A lamb upon the altar
An eagle flying

1.question: How does God make Jeremiah before his enemies (1:18)?
options: A tall tower, wall of gold, and gates of pure silver
A fortified city, iron pillar, and walls of bronze
An unshakable mountain, eternal rock, and an invisible shield
A strong rod of justice and a royal scepter of power

2.title: The broken cisterns
2.text: God recalls Israel's bridal love in the wilderness.

2.question: According to 2:2, what does God fondly remember?
options: The victories and the conquests of the people in the desert
The kindness and love of Israel's espousals
The faithfulness and obedience of the ancient priests
The many offerings brought to the sacred temple

2.question: According to 2:11, the people changed their glory for?
options: An alliance with powerful foreign nations
That which does not profit (idols)
Riches and treasures stored up in Jerusalem
The wisdom of the wise men of Egypt

2.question: What are the two evils of the people (2:13)?
options: They abandoned the sacred temple and built strange altars in the field
They forsook the fountain of living waters and hewed broken cisterns
They forgot the law of Moses and followed the customs of pagan neighbors
They denied the prophets and worshiped images of molten metal

2.question: According to 2:19, what corrects the people?
options: The strength of neighboring armies
Their own wickedness
The laws imposed by foreign kings
The famine ravaging the land

2.question: How does God say He planted Israel (2:21)?
options: As a thorn
As a noble vine
As a weed
As a thistle

2.question: According to 2:28, Judah's gods were as many as?
options: The stars
Its cities
The nations
The kings

2.question: According to 2:36, of whom will the people be ashamed, as once of Assyria?
options: Babylon
Egypt
Moab
Edom

3.title: Return unto me
3.text: Despite the unfaithfulness, God calls the people back.

3.question: How does the people call God in 3:4?
options: Strong Lord, my mighty defender of the city
My father, the guide of my youth
Powerful king, savior of all the people
Severe judge of all my sins

3.question: According to 3:11, who proved more righteous?
options: Treacherous Judah
Backsliding Israel
Both equally
Neither

3.question: According to 3:16, what will they no longer remember in those days?
options: The sacred mountain of Sinai
The ark of the covenant
The tablets of the ancient law
The golden calf idol

3.question: What does God promise to heal (3:22)?
options: The deep wounds of the sick body
The backslidings (apostasies)
The debts of the poor of the land
The droughts of the season

3.question: What does the people confess in 3:25?
options: That they faithfully kept the commandments
That they sinned against the Lord
That they were deceived by the false prophets
That they suffered unjustly

4.title: Wash thine heart
4.text: Jeremiah pleads for true repentance before the evil from the north.

4.question: From where does the evil God announces come (4:6)?
options: The south
The north
The sea
The west

4.question: What did the false prophets say (4:10)?
options: 'The sword comes'
'Ye shall have peace'
'Flee'
'Repent'

4.question: What must Jerusalem wash to be saved (4:14)?
options: The garments of all impurity
The heart from wickedness
The feet from the wrong path
The hands stained with blood

4.question: What does the prophet feel before the war (4:19)?
options: Great relief in his own strength
Pain in his heart (anguish)
Confidence in the walls of the city
Pride in his own victory

4.question: How did Jeremiah see the earth in the vision (4:23)?
options: Full of ripe fruit, and the fields all in full bloom
Without form and void, and the heavens without light
Full of many people, and all the great cities in festival
Green and fertile, completely full of abundant life

4.question: What good does it do for Jerusalem to adorn herself (4:30)?
options: Much; her allies always protect her
None; her lovers despise her
Everything; her enemies flee in terror
Little; the people rejoice

5.title: One just man
5.text: God would seek one just man to pardon the city, but finds none.

5.question: What did God seek in Jerusalem to pardon her (5:1)?
options: A mighty king able to subdue the enemies
One who does justice and seeks the truth
A fortified city able to withstand the siege
An army made ready for the holy war

5.question: Why would God not pardon them (5:7)?
options: Because they refused to pay tribute to the priests
Because they forsook Him and swore by false gods
Because they abandoned the sacrifices at the holy temple
Because they despised the ancient law of Moses

5.question: What nation will God bring from afar (5:15)?
options: A young and weak nation, very easy to defeat
An ancient, mighty nation of strange tongue
An allied nation that would come to help immediately
A neighboring nation, entirely peaceful

5.question: How is the people described in 5:21?
options: Wise, with very keen eyes and ears that listen quite well
Foolish, with eyes that see not and ears that hear not
Just, God-fearing and always very obedient to the prophets
Faithful and always ready to keep the commandments

5.question: What boundary did God set for the sea (5:22)?
options: Mountains
The sand
Walls
Islands

5.question: What did the prophets do, and the people love (5:31)?
options: Prophesy truth
Prophesy falsely
Keep silent
Fast

6.title: The old paths
6.text: The siege draws near; God calls the people back to the good way.

6.question: From where does the evil against Jerusalem appear (6:1)?
options: The south
The north
The desert
The sea

6.question: How are the people's ears described (6:10)?
options: Attentive and always ready to listen
Uncircumcised (they cannot hearken)
Open to the voice of the true prophets
Wise and full of discernment

6.question: What did they say, when there was none (6:14)?
options: 'War, war; when there is very fierce war'
'Peace, peace; when there is no peace'
'Famine, famine; when there is no famine'
'Full justice reigns here now'

6.question: What is found by walking the old paths, the good way (6:16)?
options: Lasting wealth and fame
Rest for the soul
Glory among all men
Power over nations

6.question: How is the people that comes from the north (6:23)?
options: Gentle and willing to make a covenant of peace
Cruel and without mercy (voice like the sea)
Small in number and very easy to stop and defeat
A faithful friend that always brought help

6.question: What shall the people be called (6:30)?
options: Highly polished bronze
Reprobate silver
Very precious metal
Valuable copper

7.title: The temple sermon
7.text: God condemns false trust in the temple while the people sin.

7.question: In what false words did the people trust (7:4)?
options: 'We are truly children of Abraham, we are saved'
'The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord'
'The covenant always protects us, we fear nothing'
'The sacrifice truly always purifies us'

7.question: What had the Lord's house become in their eyes (7:11)?
options: A house of business
A den of robbers
A forgotten temple
An empty fortress

7.question: What place does God give as an example of what He'll do to the house (7:12)?
options: Babylon
Shiloh
Hebron
Bethel

7.question: To whom did the people make cakes (7:18)?
options: To the gods of Egypt
The queen of heaven
To the stars of heaven
To the rising sun

7.question: What did God command the fathers when bringing them from Egypt (7:23)?
options: Keep all the yearly feasts with fervor
Obey His voice (be His people)
Multiply the daily sacrifices at the altar
Build fortified cities across the land

7.question: What abomination did they do in Topheth (7:31)?
options: Sacrifice unclean animals there
Burn their children in the fire
Worship idols made of golden wood
Dance wildly before the altars

7.question: What shall cease from the cities of Judah (7:34)?
options: The sound of great feasts and joyful gatherings
The voice of mirth (of bridegroom and bride)
The song of the Levites in the sacred temple
The noise of the weekly market in the square

8.title: Is there no balm in Gilead?
8.text: The people persist in deceit and do not repent.

8.question: What do the birds know, but the people do not (8:7)?
options: The season of the rains and the time of the harvest
Their appointed times / the judgment of the Lord
The way to the promised land and the law of Moses
The precise day of the Messiah's coming

8.question: What did they say, healing the hurt slightly (8:11)?
options: 'Rejoice greatly, for the Lord has forgiven'
'Peace, peace; when there is no peace'
'Fear not, the enemy has already fled'
'Rejoice, it is already too late'

8.question: What does God say there is no more of (8:13)?
options: Water in the spring nor bread in the barn
Grapes on the vine nor figs on the fig tree
Wheat in the barn nor oil in the press
Milk in the flock nor honey on the rock

8.question: What famous question does Jeremiah ask (8:22)?
options: 'Is there no physician in Judah?'
'Is there no balm in Gilead?'
'Where is the cure for my people?'
'Is there no remedy here?'

9.title: The weeping prophet
9.text: Jeremiah wishes to weep without ceasing for his people's ruin.

9.question: To what is the people's tongue compared (9:3)?
options: A spear for war
A bow for lies
A veil hiding truth
A flood of rain

9.question: What will God make Jerusalem (9:11)?
options: A blooming garden, a home for birds
Heaps of stones, a den of dragons
An impregnable fortress, a city of kings
A prosperous market full of life

9.question: What will God give this people to eat and drink (9:15)?
options: Sweet milk and purest honey
Wormwood and water of gall
Fresh bread and abundant new wine
Pure water and good wheat

9.question: Who is called to raise the lament (9:17)?
options: The elders of the people (wise men)
The mourning women (skilful)
The musicians of the temple (Levites)
The prophets of the Lord

9.question: In what should a man glory (9:24)?
options: In the law given to Moses
In knowing the Lord
In the mighty deeds of the king
In the Lord's temple

10.title: The idol and the living God
10.text: A contrast between mute idols and the Lord, the everlasting King.

10.question: To what are the idols compared (10:5)?
options: A leafy tree standing in an open field
A scarecrow (upright in a cucumber field)
A pillar of fire in the wilderness
A stone altar upon the hill

10.question: How is the Lord described, in contrast to idols (10:10)?
options: An idol of silver and gold, the work of craftsmen's hands
The living God and the everlasting King (the truth)
A tree adorned with blue and purple garments
A wise man among the nations, full of understanding

10.question: Who made the earth by power and wisdom (10:12)?
options: The angels of the Lord of hosts
The Lord (the portion of Jacob)
The wise men of all the nations
The princes of Judah

10.question: Whose it is not to direct his own steps (10:23)?
options: God's
Man's
The king's
The prophet's

10.question: Why were the flocks scattered (10:21)?
options: Because of the great drought that ravaged the land
Because the shepherds did not seek the Lord
Because enemies came from the north with a great army
By direct order of the king himself

11.title: The broken covenant
11.text: God recalls the covenant the people abandoned.

11.question: Cursed is he who hears not what (11:3)?
options: To the idols of Baal and Ashtoreth
The words of this covenant
To the counsel of the wicked priests
To the gods of their fathers

11.question: What did the people break (11:10)?
options: The oath made to the priests
God's covenant
The law given to Moses
Fasting and offerings

11.question: Judah's gods were as many as (11:13)?
options: The stars
Its cities
The nations
The kings

11.question: To what does Jeremiah compare himself, before those who plot against him (11:19)?
options: To a wounded eagle in full flight
A lamb brought to the slaughter
To a lion caught in a trap
To an olive tree felled by the wind

11.question: Who wanted to kill Jeremiah (11:21)?
options: The priests of Jerusalem
The men of Anathoth
The princes of the royal court
The false prophets

12.title: Why do the wicked prosper?
12.text: One of Jeremiah's confessions and God's challenging answer.

12.question: What question does Jeremiah ask God (12:1)?
options: Why do the righteous suffer so much affliction?
Why does the way of the wicked prosper?
When will famine cease upon all the land?
When will the captives return to the land?

12.question: What image does God use about greater hardships (12:5)?
options: Facing starving lions in the wilderness of the Negev
Contending with horses (and the swelling of Jordan)
Crossing the Red Sea in the midst of a raging storm
Carrying heavy burdens along the desert way

12.question: What did the people sow and reap (12:13)?
options: They sowed good seed and reaped a curse
They sowed wheat and reaped thorns
They planted vineyards and reaped bitterness
They tilled the land and reaped nothing

12.question: What will God do after plucking up the evil neighbors (12:15)?
options: Raise up new kings to govern them
Have compassion and bring them back
Send prophets to warn them
Abandon them completely

13.title: The linen girdle
13.text: A sign-act about the pride of Judah that will rot.

13.question: What object does Jeremiah hide by the Euphrates (13:1-4)?
options: An earthen vessel
A linen girdle
A scroll of parchment
An almond rod

13.question: What does the rotted girdle represent (13:9)?
options: The idolatry of Israel (that will be punished)
The pride of Judah (that will rot)
The famine that will ravage all Jerusalem
The captivity in foreign lands

13.question: With what will God fill the inhabitants of the land (13:13)?
options: Great confusion
Drunkenness
Deep anguish
Deep sorrow

13.question: What falls from the head of the king and queen (13:18)?
options: The ornament of their royal robes
The crown of their glory
The seal of their royal authority
The throne of their power

13.question: What image shows the people cannot do good (13:23)?
options: The Euphrates River flowing back to its former course
The Ethiopian changing his skin, the leopard his spots
The serpent exchanging its bitter venom for sweet honey
The desert blossoming without any rain

13.question: What does Jeremiah ask Jerusalem (13:27)?
options: 'Will you not repent?'
'Wilt thou not be made clean?'
'Will you not return to me?'
'Will you not hear me?'

14.title: The great drought
14.text: Before the drought, the people cry, but God says not to pray for them.

14.question: What is this word of the Lord about (14:1)?
options: The fall of Jerusalem
The great drought
The captivity in Babylon
The enemy invasion

14.question: What does God tell Jeremiah about praying for them (14:11)?
options: To pray without ceasing for them
Not to pray for this people
To gather the priests and intercede
To ask the people for rain

14.question: What does God say of the prophets who promise peace (14:14)?
options: That they are true messengers sent by God to comfort
That they prophesy falsely; He sent them not
That they speak with authority given directly by the Lord
That they are faithful prophets, though stern

14.question: Who sends rain, according to the people (14:22)?
options: The vanities of the gentiles, according to the priests
The Lord (not the vanities of the gentiles)
The idols of Baal, according to the false prophets
The stars of heaven, according to the diviners

15.title: A wall of bronze
15.text: Not even great intercessors would change the sentence; Jeremiah is strengthened.

15.question: Who, even if interceding, would not change the sentence (15:1)?
options: David and Solomon
Moses and Samuel
Abraham and Isaac
Elijah and Elisha

15.question: How does Jeremiah lament his birth (15:10)?
options: 'A man of blessing and abundance'
'A man of strife and contention'
'A man full of honor and glory'
'A man of peace and rest'

15.question: What did Jeremiah do with God's words (15:16)?
options: Hid them away for the day of anguish
Ate them (they were the joy of his heart)
Preached them aloud at the city gates
Tore them because of his sorrow

15.question: How does God make Jeremiah against the people (15:20)?
options: A sharpened sword of solid iron
A fortified wall of bronze
A heavy shield made of gold
A tower of watchful guard

16.title: No marriage, no mourning
16.text: Jeremiah's own life becomes a sign of the imminent judgment.

16.question: What does God forbid Jeremiah (16:2)?
options: To eat meat and drink wine throughout the city
To marry and have children (in that place)
To leave the city without the king's permission
To speak publicly about the drought

16.question: Why would the evil come upon the people (16:11-12)?
options: Because they worshiped foreign idols in the temple
Because they forsook God and His law
Because they refused to pay tithes to the Lord
Because they despised the prophets

16.question: The new oath will be about God bringing them from where (16:15)?
options: The land of Canaan
The land of the north
The mountains of the east
The distant islands of the sea

16.question: What will the nations say about the inherited idols (16:19)?
options: That they inherited great power and riches
That they inherited only lies and vanity
That they received wisdom from their fathers
That they gained divine protection

17.title: Blessed is he who trusts in the Lord
17.text: The deceitful heart and the blessing of trust in God.

17.question: Who is blessed, according to 17:7?
options: He who fears the king of Judah
He who trusts in the Lord
He who faithfully follows the priests
He who is righteous before men

17.question: How is the heart, according to 17:9?
options: Firm and unchanging forever
Deceitful, above all things
Full of pure and perfect wisdom
Upright and always very sincere

17.question: What does Jeremiah ask in 17:14?
options: Vengeance against all those who persecute him
Healing and salvation (thou art my praise)
Protection from his enemies and persecutors
Rest from all his prophetic labors

17.question: What does God command to keep in 17:21-22?
options: The solemn fast held every single week
The sabbath (no carrying burdens)
The daily offerings of grain and oil
The vows made unto the Lord

17.question: The blessing for keeping the sabbath: the city will be (17:24-25)?
options: Rebuilt in great glory
Inhabited forever
Surrounded by strong walls
Free from every enemy

18.title: The potter and the clay
18.text: At the potter's house, God teaches His sovereignty and the power of repentance.

18.question: The house of Israel is, in God's hand, like (18:6)?
options: The gold in the blacksmith's hand
The clay in the potter's hand
The stone in the mason's hand
The iron in the hot forge

18.question: If a nation turns, what does God do (18:8)?
options: Hardens the heart against it forever
Relents of the evil He thought to do
Increases the punishment already planned
Sends the full destruction at once

18.question: What do the enemies plot against Jeremiah (18:18)?
options: Arrest him and expel him from the city forever
To smite him with the tongue (a plot against him)
Accuse him falsely before the great king of Judah
Carry him captive off to Babylon at once

18.question: What did they do to Jeremiah, though he interceded for them (18:20)?
options: Gave him gold and honors as a reward
Dug a pit for him (evil for good)
Offered him protection against his pursuers
Listened to him with respect and awe

19.title: The broken bottle
19.text: Jeremiah breaks a bottle in the valley of Hinnom as a sign of ruin.

19.question: What abomination did they do in the high places of Baal (19:5)?
options: Sacrifice unclean animals to the idol
Burn their children in the fire
Dance naked before the image of Baal
Offer wine to their idols

19.question: What does Jeremiah break as a sign (19:10-11)?
options: A heavy wooden yoke
A potter's bottle
A forged rod of iron
A silver vessel

19.question: Why will God bring the evil on the city (19:15)?
options: Because they worshiped foreign idols without fear
Because they hardened their neck, not to hear
Because they totally abandoned the ancient covenant
Because they robbed and oppressed the poor

20.title: Fire in the bones
20.text: Pashur strikes Jeremiah; the prophet struggles between pain and the word that burns in him.

20.question: Who struck Jeremiah and put him in the stocks (20:1-3)?
options: Amaziah, the priest
Pashur, the priest
Malachi, the Levite
Shemaiah, the false prophet

20.question: What was God's word in Jeremiah like (20:9)?
options: Calm cool water running through his veins
A burning fire shut up in his bones
A soft cool wind blowing in his heart
A happy song upon his own lips

20.question: What does Jeremiah curse, in his anguish (20:14)?
options: The year he got married
The day he was born
The place where he was born
His own baptism

21.title: Life and death
21.text: Zedekiah inquires of Jeremiah about Babylon; the answer is harsh.

21.question: About whom does Zedekiah inquire of Jeremiah (21:2)?
options: The Egyptian pharaoh (a possible alliance)
Nebuchadnezzar (the war of Babylon)
The king of Assyria (an old and ancient fear)
The neighboring Philistines, hostile

21.question: According to 21:8-9, who goes out and surrenders to the Chaldees?
options: Will die soon (will lose everything in battle)
Will live (his life for a prey)
Will be captured and taken away for good
Will perish soon from famine and plague

21.question: What does God command the house of David to do (21:12)?
options: Rebuild the temple and the sacred altar
Execute justice and deliver the oppressed
Strengthen the army against the enemies
Renew all the ancient covenants

22.title: A word to the royal house
22.text: Justice to the oppressed — or ruin for unjust kings.

22.question: What does God command the king to do (22:3)?
options: War and conquest, to subdue all the surrounding nations
Judgment and justice (deliver the oppressed)
Taxes and tribute (to enrich the temple treasury)
Sacrifices and offerings in the temple

22.question: Why did the Lord do this to the city (22:9)?
options: Because they refused to pay tribute to the king of Babylon
Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord
Because they allied themselves with Egypt against the Lord's will
Because they defiled the temple with pagan sacrifices

22.question: Woe to him who builds his house with (22:13)?
options: Riches (without caring for the poor of the land)
Unrighteousness (without paying the worker)
Pride (seeking honor and fame among the princes)
Precious wood brought from Lebanon

22.question: How shall Jehoiakim be buried (22:19)?
options: With great pomp and royal honor
With the burial of an ass
Beside his fathers in Jerusalem
Far from the city, in a simple tent

22.question: From his youth, what did the people do (22:21)?
options: Always obeyed the prophets sent to them
Never obeyed the voice of God
Faithfully kept the covenant of the Lord
Sought righteousness with all their heart

22.question: What is written of Coniah (Jeconiah) (22:30)?
options: That he will return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple of the Lord
That he is childless (none of his seed will reign)
That he will be restored to the throne and his sons will reign forever
That he will be freed from the long Babylonian captivity

23.title: The righteous Branch
23.text: Against the false shepherds and prophets, God promises the righteous King.

23.question: What Branch will God raise to David, called 'The Lord Our Righteousness' (23:5-6)?
options: An evil Branch (a false king)
A righteous Branch (King)
A cruel Branch (a tyrant)
A new priest (a messenger)

23.question: Of what is the land full (23:10)?
options: The just
Adulterers
Prophets
Kings

23.question: The false prophets speak the vision of (23:16)?
options: The mouth of the false priests
Their own heart
Dreams sent by Baal
The wise men of Jerusalem

23.question: Can anyone hide from God (23:24)?
options: Yes, if he hides in dark caverns
No (He fills heaven and earth)
Sometimes, when man's faith is weak
At night, far from the temple light

23.question: What did the false prophets claim (23:25)?
options: 'We saw glorious angels descend from the sky'
'I have dreamed, I have dreamed' (lies)
'We heard the sacred law given to Moses'
'We fasted seven days in the temple'

23.question: The true prophet speaks the word with (23:28)?
options: Dreams (vain visions of the human heart)
Truth (the chaff is not the wheat)
Fear (seeking favor with the princes)
Silence before the multitudes

23.question: God's word is like (23:29)?
options: Strong wind that scatters the dry chaff
Fire and a hammer that breaks the rock
Still water reflecting a calm and quiet sky
Light smoke that fades into the air

23.question: What expression does God forbid to use mockingly (23:33)?
options: 'The wrath of the Lord God'
'The burden of the Lord'
'The final judgment of the Lord'
'The sword of the Lord God'

24.title: The two baskets of figs
24.text: The good figs are the exiles; the bad, those who remained.

24.question: What do the good figs represent (24:5)?
options: Israel's enemies (who will be destroyed forever)
Judah's captives (whom God will treat for good)
Judah's kings (who will judge the people with justice)
The false prophets who deceive all the people

24.question: What do the bad figs represent (24:8-10)?
options: The exiles who will return to rebuild the ruined land of Judah
Zedekiah and those who remained (sword, famine, pestilence)
The righteous ones who remained faithful and true within the sacred temple
The priests who served faithfully in the temple

25.title: The seventy years
25.text: Jeremiah announces the captivity and the cup of fury to the nations.

25.question: For how many years did Jeremiah preach unheard (25:3)?
options: Thirty-seven years
Twenty-three years
One hundred and twenty years
Twelve and a half years

25.question: For how many years will the nations serve Babylon (25:11)?
options: Forty years
Seventy years
A hundred years
Seven years

25.question: What cup does Jeremiah give the nations (25:15)?
options: The cup of consolation and hope
The cup of fury (wine of wrath)
The cup of blessing and restoration
The cup of everlasting joy

25.question: What happens after the seventy years (25:12)?
options: Judah will be restored immediately
God will punish Babylon herself
All nations will live in eternal peace
Israel will become enslaved again

25.question: Who drinks the cup first (25:18)?
options: Egypt and all of Pharaoh's princes
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah
Edom, Moab, and the children of Ammon
All the kings of the land of Uz

25.question: How will the Lord manifest Himself against the land (25:30)?
options: He will whisper among the clouds
He will roar from on high
He will send a sign in the sky
He will speak in secret

25.question: Whom does Jeremiah tell to howl, for the days of slaughter have come (25:34)?
options: The kings
The shepherds
The prophets
The wise

25.question: To what is the Lord compared, leaving his covert (25:38)?
options: A wild bull calf
A young lion
A ravenous bear
A fierce wolf

26.title: Jeremiah's trial
26.text: For the temple sermon, Jeremiah is threatened with death, but acquitted.

26.question: To what place does God compare the house, if they do not obey (26:6)?
options: Babylon
Shiloh
Bethel
Hebron

26.question: What did priests and prophets want to do to Jeremiah (26:8-11)?
options: Banish him from the holy city
Kill him (worthy of death)
Imprison him in the king's house
Judge him before the people

26.question: What did the princes and people decide (26:16)?

That Jeremiah should be expelled from the city

Micah

options: To Zedekiah, the very king of Judah
Nebuchadnezzar (His servant)
To Pharaoh of Egypt and his princes
To the kings of neighboring nations

Will remain in its land

The prophets who say they will not serve Babylon

Until the day God visits them
Until the end of Zedekiah's reign

That Babylon's yoke will be broken in two years

Iron yokes
No yoke

He received forgiveness from the LORD

Build houses and plant gardens
Fast and mourn continually in exile
Wage war against the Babylonians

Seventy
Ten
Seven

Of peace, and not of evil (hope)
Of abandonment and total forgetfulness
Of judgment and final condemnation

options: When they offer sacrifices every single day
When they seek Him with all their heart
When they consult the stars and diviners
When they fast for many consecutive days

options: The corrupt priests among the Babylonians
The false prophets and diviners
The exiled princes living in Babylon

options: Baruch, the son of Neriah the scribe
Shemaiah the Nehelamite
Gedaliah, son of Ahikam the governor
Uriah, son of Shemaiah

30.title: The Book of Consolation
30.text: God promises to bring Israel and Judah back from captivity.

30.question: According to 30:7, though the day of Jacob's trouble is great, he will be?
options: Consumed within it
Saved out of it
Multiplied inside it
Left all alone

30.question: Whom will they serve, according to 30:9?
options: The princes of Babylon and their gods
The Lord and David their king
Pharaoh of Egypt and his priests
The idols of neighboring nations

Restore health and heal it
Deepen the wound even further
Cover the wound with dirty cloth

'Ye shall be my people, and I will be your God'
'Never again will you remember my holy name at all'

30.question: When will the purpose of the Lord's anger be fully understood (30:24)?
options: Before the captivity begins
In the latter days
On the day of harvest
After seventy years pass

31.title: The new covenant
31.text: Jeremiah's central promise: the law written on the heart.

31.question: With what love did God love Israel (31:3)?
options: A passing love
An everlasting love
A conditional love
A distant love

31.question: How is Ephraim called in 31:9?
options: A servant
My firstborn
A stranger
An enemy

31.question: Into what will God turn the people's mourning (31:13)?
options: Silence
Joy
More mourning
Fear

31.question: Who weeps for her children in Ramah (31:15)?
options: Sarah
Rachel
Deborah
Hannah

31.question: How does God call Ephraim in 31:20?
options: A rejected servant (a cause of eternal shame)
A precious son (the child of His delight)
An ungrateful son (a heavy burden to his father)
A stranger with no place in his heart

31.question: Why will each one die, according to 31:30?
options: For the sins of the whole nation
For his own iniquity
For the transgression of his neighbors
For an inherited curse

31.question: Where will God put His law in the new covenant (31:33)?
options: On sacred scrolls kept safely hidden away
In their inward parts and on their hearts
On the walls of the newly rebuilt temple courts
On the ancient altars used for sacrifice

Forgive and remember them no more
Announce them publicly to all the people

32.title: The purchase of the field
32.text: During the siege, Jeremiah buys a field — an act of faith in restoration.

32.question: Why had Zedekiah imprisoned Jeremiah (32:2-3)?
options: For advising a secret alliance with Egypt against Babylon
For prophesying the city's surrender to Babylon
For refusing to hand over the scriptures to the king
For inciting the people to flee the besieged city

32.question: What does Jeremiah buy as a sign of hope (32:9)?
options: A house in the city of Jerusalem
A field in Anathoth
A flock of sheep in Benjamin
A well of water

32.question: What does the purchase of the field mean (32:15)?

Houses and fields shall be bought again in the land (restoration)
The permanent flight of the whole people to Egypt, never to return again
The permanent cancellation of the covenant with Israel

That nothing is too hard for Him (He made heaven and earth)
That He has permanently abandoned the people because of sin
That He now regrets all the promises made to Israel

The siege mounts of the Chaldees
Signs of retreat by the Babylonian army
A great famine in the city

options: The Lord, the God of the heavenly hosts
The Lord, the God of all flesh
The Lord, the avenging God of Israel
The god of the Chaldeans and Egyptians

Turned their back to Him, and not the face
Turned back to Him with humility and repentance

options: A conditional covenant (depending fully on their obedience)
An everlasting covenant (He will not turn away from them)
A covenant to be renewed with each new generation of Israel

32.question: What will they do again in the land (32:44)?
options: Build many pagan temples (a sign of continued rebellion)
Buy fields (God will bring them back from captivity)
Abandon the promised land for good (permanent exile)
Make war against the Babylonians once more

33.title: Call unto me
33.text: Still imprisoned, Jeremiah receives the promise of healing and the righteous Branch.

33.question: What does God promise to him who calls on Him (33:3)?
options: Great riches and immediate material prosperity
To answer and show great and hidden things
Immediate and complete victory over all his enemies
Absolute silence until the day of judgment

options: Famine, war, and complete destruction
Health, cure, and abundance of peace
Permanent exile and no return ever again
More plagues and great affliction

33.question: What Branch of righteousness will God grow to David (33:15-16)?
options: A temporary Branch ('Servant of the King of Babylon')
The righteous Branch ('The Lord Our Righteousness')
A foreign Branch, named 'Great Prince of the Chaldeans'
A minor prophet with no royal descendants

33.question: The seed of David will be multiplied like (33:22)?
options: The grains of sand in the whole desert of Egypt
The host of heaven and the sand of the sea
The leaves of the trees throughout the whole world
The stones of the temple of Solomon

33.question: To what is God's faithfulness compared (33:20-25)?
options: The covenant made with the angels of heaven
The covenant of day and night
The oath made only to the priests
The strength of the eternal mountains

34.title: The broken liberty
34.text: The people free the Hebrew slaves and then turn back.

options: That he will be killed by the sword of the Chaldeans
That he will not die by the sword, but in peace
That he will reign in peace for many years still

options: Pay tribute to the king of Babylon
To free the Hebrew slaves
Build a new temple in Jerusalem
Surrender himself to the king of Babylon

options: Kept the liberty they had promised the servants
Turned back and enslaved them again
Fled all together to the neighboring lands

The sword, the pestilence, and the famine

35.title: The Rechabites
35.text: The Rechabites' obedience shames Judah's disobedience.

options: Water
Wine
Milk
New wine

In obedience to their father Jonadab
From fear of the armies surrounding the city
By an ancient law of the kingdom

Did not obey God
Fled to foreign lands
Prayed secretly each day

35.question: What blessing do the Rechabites receive (35:19)?

They will never lack a man before the Lord
A great and prosperous kingdom lasting forever
A great temple dedicated to the Lord

Baruch
Pashur
Hananiah

So they may turn and He may forgive
For a historical record of the events

Cuts it and burns it in the brazier

Completely different words from before

In the royal palace with the princes
